processing.aspectConvention: degrees clockwise from true north (UTM grid aspect plus meridian convergence at the cell centre); -1 flat

limitations: Slope classes describe steepness only. They are not a hazard rating and do not say whether any slope is safe to ski.

Computed from a 10 m grid resampled from the USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second DEM. Features smaller than about 20-30 m (cliff bands, gullies, cornices, rollovers) are smoothed or missing; short steep pitches can be steeper than shown.
Snow depth, wind loading and cornices change the real surface; this is bare-earth terrain.
Aspect is degrees clockwise from true north: computed on the UTM 13N grid, then corrected by the meridian convergence at each cell (0.39-0.65 degrees in the pilot).

numeric.tileScheme: utm-block (NOT Web Mercator; never add as a map source)
numeric.aspect: degrees clockwise from true north; the decoder adds the meridian convergence at the cell centre (utmConvergenceDeg)
numeric.encoding: zlib(byte planes 0..3 of uint32 LE zigzag(2-D difference residuals of int elevation)); elevation_m = n / elevScale
